item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-05cb1f67cd4af71f","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In May 2023, the CENI publicly announced a mixed national and international external audit mission for the voter register and identified selected experts, including experienced electoral administrators, statisticians, legal specialists, and election observers from the DRC and other African countries.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.10","8B.4"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; concerns the electoral process under Tshisekedi's presidency, although the source attributes the action to the CENI rather than personally to Tshisekedi.","ruler_attribution":"Institutional action by the CENI; no direct presidential order is stated.","limitations":["The document announces the experts and their qualifications but does not report the audit's findings or independence in practice."]},{"source_id":"SRC-67f4a8d2fc1fd355","start_unit":20,"end_unit":21,"fact_summary":"During the December 20, 2023 elections, UDPS supporters, whose party was led by President Félix Tshisekedi, punched, dragged, and threw journalist Pascal Mulegwa into a gutter in Kinshasa; he reported that attackers accused him of working for a French outlet critical of Tshisekedi and broke his glasses. The communications minister sent transport to take him to hospital, but CPJ reported no response from the UDPS secretary general or minister to its accountability inquiries.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within December 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The attack is attributed to UDPS supporters; the source does not state that Tshisekedi personally ordered or endorsed it. The minister's assistance is a government response, while the alleged attackers' accountability remained unresolved in the report.","limitations":["The account relies on media reports and interviews; the article does not establish the attackers' formal authority or a completed investigation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-67f4a8d2fc1fd355","start_unit":21,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"On December 16, 2023, AREP supporters in Mankanza attacked Radio Liberté Mankanza editor-in-chief Réné Mobembo while he covered an AREP campaign meeting; about seven supporters punched him, confiscated his cellphone, and he sought hospital treatment. The same report states that the media regulator ordered Perfect Télévision off air on December 20 after its reports on delayed polling-station openings and missing electoral kits; the station remained off air on December 22.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly within December 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The violence is attributed to AREP supporters and the broadcast shutdown to the CSAC; the source does not establish direct presidential authorization.","limitations":["The report does not establish whether Tshisekedi personally knew of, ordered, or later remedied either incident."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1edc2c6f87a2ea28","start_unit":20,"end_unit":21,"fact_summary":"In late July 2023, at least seven journalists were assaulted in three election-related incidents. In one incident, the federal president of the MLC, a party allied with Tshisekedi, and three MLC militants allegedly broke journalist José Nkoso's windows and doors and beat him with sticks after an interview suggested MLC candidates would lose; the deputy government administrator said the four alleged assailants were arrested but that the MLC leader was later released.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","7B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly within July 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The alleged perpetrators included a leader of a party allied with Tshisekedi; the source does not attribute the attack to Tshisekedi personally.","limitations":["The article reports allegations and an ongoing investigation; it does not state the final legal outcome or any presidential response."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1edc2c6f87a2ea28","start_unit":22,"end_unit":23,"fact_summary":"On July 29, 2023, supporters of opposition candidate Martin Fayulu allegedly slapped and manhandled journalist Frank Kalonji and took his phone during coverage of an ECIDé rally. The same day, suspected ruling-party supporters blocked access to an opposition rally in Kananga by setting tires alight, barricading roads, and throwing stones; the candidate and three journalists sustained minor head injuries. Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya condemned the attack and said those responsible would be brought to justice.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within July 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The Kananga attackers were described as suspected ruling-party supporters; the source records a government condemnation but not Tshisekedi's personal involvement or a completed prosecution.","limitations":["The identities of some attackers and the eventual accountability outcome were not established in the source."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2838ae4d4dd03fe5","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"ACLED reported that April 2023 ceasefire agreements with M23 reduced hostilities for several months, but their breakdown in October was followed by a 29% increase in political violence involving M23 compared with 2022. M23 gained more territory in 2023, while the Congolese army's strategy of supporting and fighting alongside non-state armed groups risked arming potential adversaries.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.5","2B.7","2B.10","3B.6","3B.9","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The reported conflict trends and ceasefire effects concern 2023; the article was published in January 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The source discusses Kinshasa's security strategy and negotiations but does not assign each military decision directly to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The source synthesizes conflict data and secondary reporting; it does not provide a complete account of government orders, civilian-protection enforcement, or responsibility for the ceasefire breakdown."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2838ae4d4dd03fe5","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The ADF was responsible for over 1,000 reported fatalities in the DRC in 2023, and fatalities from its cross-border violence into Uganda doubled compared with the previous year.","question_ids":["2B.10","3B.6","3B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The outcome occurred during Tshisekedi's presidency, but the source does not establish his personal responsibility for ADF attacks or the precise effect of government policy.","limitations":["The figure is reported fatalities, not necessarily a complete casualty count; causal attribution to presidential policy is not established."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2838ae4d4dd03fe5","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"ACLED reported that demonstrations against the electoral process and violence targeting electoral workers, offices, and materials increased during the 2023 voting period, while the contested election produced unrest, violence against perceived illegitimate winners, and suppression of political opposition by those in power.","question_ids":["3B.8","3B.9","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.10","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the December 2023 election period.","ruler_attribution":"The source describes actions by political groups and those in power but does not specify which incidents were personally directed by Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The report provides an analytical summary rather than a complete incident-level attribution or legal finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a9df98ecc8808dee","start_unit":11,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"In October 2023, RSF reported that journalist Stanis Bujakera Tshiamala had been detained since September 8 and urged presidential candidates to support dropping charges against him and other arbitrarily detained journalists. RSF recorded 123 arbitrary arrests of journalists from June 2020 to September 2023, three journalists murdered in prior years, and ranked the DRC 124th of 180 countries in its 2023 World Press Freedom Index; it proposed ten press-freedom commitments for candidates, including a moratorium on work-related arrests, investigations of murders, media-law reform, and independence of the public broadcaster and regulator.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The detention and advocacy occurred in 2023; the historical arrest and murder totals cover earlier periods.","ruler_attribution":"RSF addressed all presidential candidates, including Tshisekedi, but the source does not state whether he signed or implemented the proposed commitments.","limitations":["The source is an advocacy appeal and does not establish a final judicial finding that every cited detention was arbitrary."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c17ed62b872a40e5","start_unit":12,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"The December 2022 Nairobi-process communiqué, issued after consultations with the DRC government under Tshisekedi, committed to continued cessation of hostilities, release of child soldiers, humanitarian access, a fully funded P-DDRCS program, review of its leadership, and a public statement by Tshisekedi; it also contemplated community participation in conservation and mining decisions.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.7","2B.10","3B.7","3B.9","5B.1","5B.6","6B.3","6B.6","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The agreement was dated December 2022 but established commitments relevant to implementation during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The communiqué expressly attributes accepted commitments and a planned public statement to President Tshisekedi; it does not document completion or funding in 2023.","limitations":["The document records commitments, not verified implementation or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bac8a152bcc56527","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In May 2023, the CENI announced an external audit of the 2022–2023 voter register after detecting duplicates, minors, and invalid photographs with biometric software. The terms required a mixed national and international expert team, conflict-of-interest exclusions, assessment of inclusiveness, completeness, and accuracy, publication of results, and possible legal action for misuse of voter data.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.4","4B.6","4B.7","4B.9","4B.10","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly within May 2023 and tied to the 2023 election process.","ruler_attribution":"The measures are formally attributed to the CENI; the source states that government resources were pooled for voter identification but does not attribute the audit design personally to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The terms of reference do not establish whether the audit was completed, published, or acted upon."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7be6e07a7b881cef","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In May 2023, the CENI announced an external audit of the 2022–2023 voter register after using biometric software to detect duplicates, minors, and invalid photographs. The terms required a mixed national and international expert team, conflict-of-interest exclusions, assessment of inclusiveness, completeness, and accuracy, publication of results, and possible legal action for misuse of voter data.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.4","4B.6","4B.7","4B.9","4B.10","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly within May 2023 and tied to the 2023 election process.","ruler_attribution":"The measures are formally attributed to the CENI; the source states that government resources were pooled for voter identification but does not attribute the audit design personally to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["This is an English version of the CENI terms of reference and does not establish completion, publication, or implementation of the audit."]},{"source_id":"SRC-163c36bbd46c15c3","start_unit":10,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"Following the February 2023 EAC summit, the March 2 Joint Coordination Mechanism set a phased plan for M23 withdrawal from named locations, deployment of EAC regional-force contingents, monitoring and verification by joint mechanisms, an action plan and roadmap, regular reporting, and support from the AU Peace Fund and MONUSCO.","question_ids":["2B.7","2B.10","3B.6","3B.9","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns a March 2023 ceasefire implementation process.","ruler_attribution":"The mechanism was an EAC-led process involving the DRC government/FARDC; the document does not state that Tshisekedi personally issued the operational decisions.","limitations":["The report documents planned mechanisms and commitments, not their full execution or durability; later ACLED reporting indicates the ceasefire subsequently broke down."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-32b2d6a1537f46b7","SRC-e5ec364dabcbe82f","SRC-7696f6f97f8fc06e"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied documents contain limited direct evidence of Félix Tshisekedi's personal decisions, orders, or accountability actions; several facts concern institutions, parties, supporters, or broader outcomes during his presidency.","SRC-c17ed62b872a40e5 is dated December 2022, so its facts are included only where they establish commitments carried into the 2023 period.","SRC-2838ae4d4dd03fe5 was published in January 2024 but reports 2023 events and outcomes.","No scoring was performed."]}
